output.name: Lutha

anatomy.part: the tallow lamp set on the gunwale near the prow, the one still burning
the stern tip of the hull, where the mast is stepped
the foot of the bow, where the keel curves up
the rising stem of the prow
the masthead lantern at the top of the raked mast
the tip of the cloth streamer blowing from the masthead

output.myth: When Aun cut the string, the sky drifted off so fast that boats in the Leeward Reach lost their way. Hesk counted the missing from her pole and was not pleased. So Ennu the Kite-Wright made a lamp of tallow and bone and set it on a prow, to show a boat the way in past the rocks. Many boats came home by it. One did not. Its lamp was still burning when the wind took the boat, and it still burns, low on the Upper Sea, where the mast leans and a torn streamer flies. Tavo laughs at it every night. Sil has watched it too and says nothing, which is how she says she hopes. Keep your wick trimmed, and keep your hands on the rope.
output.verse:
One lamp, low and lit,
on the prow the salt has not
put out. Steer home by its light.
